Components: Components are the fundamental building blocks of Angular apps, each consisting of a TypeScript class, HTML template, and optional CSS styles. They control a view via a decorated class with @Component metadata.
Modules: NgModules organize an Angular app into cohesive blocks of functionality by declaring components, importing dependencies, and providing services. Every app has a root module (AppModule) as the entry point.
Templates: Angular templates extend HTML with custom syntax including interpolation ({{ }}), property binding ([ ]), event binding (( )), and structural directives (*ngIf, *ngFor) for dynamic views.

Dependency Injection: Angular's dependency injection system provides dependencies to classes via constructor parameters. The injector hierarchy creates singleton or per-component instances of services automatically.
Services: Services are singleton classes decorated with @Injectable that encapsulate business logic, data access, or cross-cutting concerns. They are the recommended way to share logic between components.
Providers: Providers configure the injector with dependency recipes, controlling how services are created and scoped. They can be registered at module level, component level, or using providedIn: 'root' for tree-shaking.

Router: Angular Router enables navigation between views in SPAs with URL-based routing, nested routes, lazy-loaded modules, and route parameters. It integrates with the browser's history API.
Lazy Loading: Lazy loading loads feature modules on demand when the user navigates to their routes, reducing initial bundle size. Use loadChildren in route config to point to a module imported via dynamic import.
Guards: Route guards control navigation using interfaces like CanActivate, CanDeactivate, and Resolve. They prevent unauthorized access, prompt for unsaved changes, and pre-fetch data before a route activates.

Template-driven: Template-driven forms rely on directives in the template like ngModel for two-way data binding. They are simpler but less scalable than reactive forms, suitable for basic form use cases.
Reactive: Reactive forms provide a model-driven approach with form control instances created programmatically, offering more predictability, testability, and advanced validation capabilities.
Validation: Angular forms support built-in validators (required, minLength, pattern) and custom async validators. Validation state is exposed through CSS classes (ng-valid, ng-invalid) and component properties.

HttpClient: HttpClient is Angular's built-in HTTP client with typed request/response, interceptors, and automatic JSON parsing. Methods return Observables supporting RxJS operators for transformations.
Interceptors: Interceptors sit between the application and the backend, transforming outgoing requests or incoming responses. Common use cases include adding auth tokens, logging, and error handling.
Error Handling: Error handling in HTTP requests is done via RxJS catchError operator, retrying failed requests, or displaying user-friendly error messages. Global error handling can be centralized in interceptors.

Directives: Angular offers three types of directives: components, structural directives (alter DOM layout), and attribute directives (change appearance or behavior). Custom directives encapsulate reusable DOM manipulation.
Pipes: Pipes transform data in templates for display, such as formatting dates, currencies, or filtering lists. Angular provides built-in pipes and you can create custom pure or impure pipes.
Custom Decorators: Decorators are TypeScript features used extensively in Angular for metadata. Custom decorators can extend component behavior, add logging, or transform class properties at design time.

Jasmine: Jasmine is a behavior-driven development framework for testing JavaScript code with a clean, readable syntax. It provides describe/it blocks, matchers (toEqual, toContain), and spies.
Karma: Karma is a test runner that executes tests in real browsers, providing fast feedback loops and reporting. It's the default test runner in Angular CLI projects via ng test.
TestBed: TestBed is Angular's primary testing utility for configuring and creating component test environments. It manages module compilation, dependency injection, and provides ComponentFixture for interaction.

Change Detection: Angular's default change detection checks every component in the tree when any data changes, ensuring consistency. It uses zone.js to patch browser APIs and trigger checks automatically.
OnPush: OnPush change detection strategy reduces unnecessary checks by only running detection when input references change, events fire, or observables emit. It's essential for large lists and performance-critical views.
Code Splitting: Angular supports code splitting through lazy-loaded modules and ES dynamic imports. The CLI generates separate chunks per lazy route, and the router loads them on demand when the user navigates.
